metaDescription: Six rice cookers that handle quinoa well, from dedicated quinoa programs to ceramic minis, with water ratios, rinsing advice and pot care compared.
expertTake: The COMFEE' 14-in-1 multicooker is the best quinoa pick here because it pairs a 10 cup uncooked pot with a long list of grain and oat programs. The IMUSA 3-cup ceramic cooker is the value pick for one or two people who list quinoa on the box. Skip a dedicated quinoa program if you cook it twice a year, because any rice cooker with a white rice cycle and the right water line will do.
introParagraphs: Quinoa is not a grain but a seed, and it behaves differently from rice. It cooks quickly, absorbs less water and carries a bitter coating that needs rinsing. A cooker that is tuned for long-grain rice can overshoot and leave quinoa mushy, which is why a quinoa program or a gentle white rice cycle matters.

The machines here range from basic one-switch mini cookers that list quinoa on the box to digital multicookers with dedicated grain programs. We evaluated them on how clearly quinoa is supported, how the pot copes with small seeds and how easily the cooker handles other grains and oats.

products.name: COMFEE' 14-in-1 Stainless Rice Cooker, 10 Cups Uncooked, 5.3 Qt

specList.label: Grain menus
specList.value: White, brown, quick, rolled and steel-cut oats

products.description:
The COMFEE' 14-in-1 is the grain generalist of this group. Fourteen digital programs cover white rice, brown rice, quick rice, rolled oats, steel-cut oats and more, so quinoa can ride the right cycle instead of being forced into a rice setting. A 5.3 quart pot can yield up to 20 cups of cooked rice or grains, and the stainless finish gives it a sturdier look than the plastic minis.

A large pot is a mixed blessing for quinoa, which is usually cooked in small amounts. A cup of quinoa makes about three cups cooked, so the cooker is wasted on a small batch, and a thin layer of seeds on a big plate can stick. Compared with the COMFEE' 6-function model, this one is the machine for a family that cooks grains in volume.

Rinse the seeds in a fine strainer before adding them, because a normal rice-cooker pot has no screen and small grains can pass through some drains. Wipe the panel with a damp cloth and clean the lid vent. The pot should be soaked after a quinoa cook, since the starch and saponin residue dry to a film. Because the pot is so large, it makes sense to cook quinoa in a double batch and freeze it flat in bags, which suits a salad or grain bowl routine. The slow cook mode is also a useful way to make a quinoa breakfast porridge with milk and fruit overnight.
products.bestFor: Families that cook quinoa, oats and rice in one machine.
pros: Slow cook, steam and saute included
cons: Big pot is wasteful for one cup of quinoa

products.name: COMFEE' 6-Function Rice Cooker, 4 Cups Uncooked, 2 Qt

specList.label: Programs
specList.value: White, brown, steam, slow cook, quinoa, oatmeal

products.description:
This is the cooker that puts quinoa on its panel. Six digital programs include white rice, brown rice, steam, slow cook, quinoa and oatmeal, and the 4 cup uncooked, 2 quart pot yields up to 8 cups cooked. For a person who eats quinoa weekly, a button with its name on it removes the water and timing guesswork.

A dedicated program is only as good as the controller behind it, and this is a fixed-program digital cooker, not a fuzzy logic machine. It does the job at a normal load, while a half-empty pot behaves less predictably. The compact size is its strength for quinoa, since a typical batch of one to two cups fits well.

After cooking, fluff with a fork and leave the lid on for five minutes so the seeds finish steaming. Rinse the quinoa until the water runs clear, because the bitter coating survives cooking if you skip it. Wipe the lid underside, and dry the pot base before the next use. Oatmeal and quinoa can share the same cooker, but wash the pot between them so the flavors do not carry over. If the unit has an LED display, a blinking code usually means the pot was not seated, so lift it out and place it again before cooking.
products.bestFor: Quinoa eaters who want a button for it in a compact pot.

products.name: IMUSA 3-Cup Uncooked Electric Ceramic Rice Cooker, White
products.description:
IMUSA sells this as a mini cooker for rice, quinoa, risotto, oatmeal, soups and stews. The removable ceramic pot is described as scratch resistant and easy to clean, and the capacity of 3 cups uncooked or 6 cups cooked suits singles, couples and students. It is a simple machine without a panel of programs.

Because there is no quinoa button, you will use the white rice cycle and a quinoa water line, which is about two parts water to one part seeds. The cycle ends when the water is gone, which is the right behavior for quinoa. For a household that wants to try quinoa without buying a digital cooker, this is the low-cost route.

Do not overfill the small pot, since quinoa expands about three times. Keep a nylon spoon with the cooker, and soak the pot after cooking. Ceramic is hard, but it can chip if knocked, so store it with care and wash by hand. Quinoa pairs well with the stew function of this mini cooker, since a pot of quinoa chili needs only one stir. Remember that the small pot leaves almost no headroom for foam, so fill the quinoa and water to no more than half.
products.bestFor: Singles and students who want a cheap cooker that also handles quinoa.
pros: Suitable for quinoa, oatmeal and stew

products.name: Narcissus 3.5-Cup Uncooked Rice Cooker, 1.8 L, PFAS-Free Pot
products.description:
Narcissus sells this as a cooker for one to three people, with 3.5 cups uncooked and a 1.8 liter pot. Programs cover white and brown rice, oatmeal and quinoa, and a delay start with automatic warm completes the schedule. The pot is removable and described as PFAS-free nonstick.

The delay start deserves a caution for quinoa: seeds soaking in water for hours can turn soft, so use the timer for only a short delay. The brand is newer, so the long-term record is thin. For a small household that wants program choices and a modest cost, it is a reasonable pick.

Rinse the quinoa in a fine strainer, measure water by the quinoa line and avoid filling beyond the mark. Wash the pot by hand with a soft sponge. Wipe the lid vent after each cook. The program list is a good start for someone moving from white rice to whole grains, because the brown rice and oatmeal menus give a gentle introduction to different water ratios. Keep the manual handy until the first few batches teach you where the lines sit.
products.bestFor: One to three people who want quinoa and brown rice programs.
pros: Programs for quinoa, brown rice and oatmeal
3.5 cups uncooked in a 1.8 L pot
cons: Newer brand with a short record

products.name: AROMA Digital 4-Cup Raw Rice and Grain Cooker, 2 Qt
products.description:
AROMA calls this a grain cooker as well as a rice cooker, and the digital panel offers white rice, brown rice, steam and flash rice presets with an automatic Keep Warm after each cycle. A steam tray stacks above the pot, so a bowl of quinoa can cook beneath while fish or vegetables steam above. The 2 quart pot takes 4 raw cups, which is a sensible ceiling for quinoa, since it swells about three times.

There is no dedicated quinoa program, so you choose the white rice preset or the brown rice preset and rely on your water measurement. Brown rice is the safer choice for whole seeds that you want firm, while white is better for a softer pot of quinoa porridge. Against the COMFEE' 6-function model, this one trades the named quinoa button for a steam tray and a longer record of ownership.

Quinoa foams more than rice when it is not rinsed, so do not skip the strainer. Wipe the underside of the lid and the steam tray after every use, and wash the pot with a soft sponge. If you use the steam tray with quinoa, check that the water level covers both foods.
products.bestFor: Cooks who steam vegetables over a pot of grains.
pros: White, brown, steam and flash presets
Steam tray stacks above the grains
Automatic Keep Warm after each cycle

products.name: Cosori 10-Cup Fuzzy Logic Rice Cooker, Ceramic Pot, 18-in-1

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: 18, white and brown with texture options

products.description:
Cosori brings fuzzy logic to grain cooking, which matters because quinoa and rice differ in how they respond to heat. Eighteen functions, including white and brown rice with texture options, a saute mode and a slow cook mode, make it the most flexible controller in this group. The pot is ceramic coated.

It is a 10 cup machine, so it shares the large-pot drawback for small quinoa batches. Where the COMFEE' 6-function cooker has a quinoa button, the Cosori relies on its adaptive heat and your water measurement. A cook who likes to choose a texture will enjoy the extra control.

Saute the quinoa dry for a minute before adding water if you like a nuttier taste, and use plastic tools in the ceramic pot. Soak the pot after cooking and wipe the vent. Let the cooker rest a few minutes before opening the lid. Mixing quinoa with rice in the same pot works, but cook them together only on a program meant for mixed grains, since quinoa finishes sooner than white rice. Toasting the seeds first is a small step that gives a nutty flavor and helps the seeds stay separate.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want adaptive heat and texture options for grains.
pros: Fuzzy logic adapts to the grain
cons: 10 cups is large for one cup of quinoa

buyingCriteria.explanation: A dedicated quinoa program, as on the COMFEE' 6-function cooker, sets time and temperature for seeds. Without one, the white rice cycle works with a quinoa water line, because it ends when the water is gone. The cooker only needs to stop at the right moment.

Quinoa takes about two parts water to one part seeds, which is more than people expect. Rice cookers often print only rice lines, so you may need to measure with a cup. A wrong ratio gives mush or hard seeds, and the error shows up quickly because quinoa is a small seed with little tolerance. Start at two to one, then adjust by a few tablespoons after the first batch to match your cooker and your taste.

Quinoa seeds carry a bitter coating called saponin, and rinsing in a fine strainer removes it. A rice cooker pot is not a strainer, and small seeds can slip through coarse drains. Rinse before the seeds go into the pot, and drain well, because extra water in the strainer adds to the pot water and loosens the ratio. A thirty second rinse under running water is enough for most packaged quinoa, though some brands are pre-rinsed and need less.

One cup of quinoa makes about three cups cooked, so a 10 cup pot like the Cosori or COMFEE' 14-in-1 is wasteful for small batches. The 3 cup IMUSA and the 3.5 cup Narcissus fit small amounts better. Match the pot to the quantity you cook.

Delay timers let grains soak in water before cooking, which suits rice. Quinoa soaked too long goes soft. Use a short delay or none. If you want quinoa ready at dinner, start it fresh when you get home, because it cooks in a fraction of the time rice needs and the pot is ready in a quarter of an hour once the heat builds.

The COMFEE' 14-in-1 lists rolled oats and steel-cut oats, and the Narcissus lists oatmeal. A cooker that handles oats and quinoa becomes a breakfast and side dish machine. Check the menu for the grains you cook.

faq.q: How much water for quinoa in a rice cooker?
faq.a: About two parts water to one part rinsed quinoa. Check the cooker manual for a specific line.

faq.q: Do I need a quinoa setting?
faq.a: No. The white rice cycle works with the right water. A quinoa program only makes the timing easier, and it matters most for people who cook quinoa every week and want one button with no measuring decisions.

Usually too much water or a long soak or delay. Measure carefully and avoid long timers. Letting the pot rest with the lid on for five minutes and fluffing with a fork also drives off surface moisture, which is the quickest rescue for a pot that looks wet.

faq.q: Do I need to rinse quinoa?
faq.a: Yes, rinsing removes the bitter saponin coating. Use a fine strainer.

faq.q: Can I cook other grains the same way?
faq.a: Many, such as millet and bulgur, with adjusted water. Check each grain's ratio.
A small or medium pot is ideal, since quinoa expands about three times and most batches are small.
